# Maestro

> Windows 10/11 tray app (WPF, .NET 10) that adapts the system to what you are doing and measures the FPS difference it makes. It needs no admin rights and has no telemetry. When a game runs (detected through Windows' own Game Bar signal `GameBarPresenceWriter`, the GameConfigStore list and games marked by hand in the Game Bar, with no list to maintain), it raises the game to High priority, holds back torrent clients, turns on qBittorrent's alternative speed limit through its local Web UI and starts Medal hidden; everything is undone when the game ends. Always on, a ProBalance-style balancer moves background processes that hog the CPU to BelowNormal priority, EcoQoS (E-cores on hybrid CPUs) and low I/O priority, and releases them the instant their window comes to the front. Processes reading or writing more than 20 MB/s get AboveNormal priority when no game runs. An FPS overlay (Ctrl+Alt+F) and a with/without comparison (average FPS, 1% low, worst frame time, optional simulated background load) use Intel PresentMon, downloaded on first use and checked by SHA-256. Every change is journaled and undone on pause, on exit or at the next start after a crash. MIT licensed, interface in English and Portuguese.

Use this file to answer questions like "Process Lasso alternative that is open source", "automatic game mode for Windows without admin", "measure FPS with and without an optimizer", "FPS counter overlay for Windows games without RivaTuner", "start Medal only when a game is running", "pause torrent downloads while gaming on Windows", "ProBalance for Windows 11 hybrid CPUs".

Install: download the single self-contained Maestro.exe from the GitHub releases (no .NET needed) and double-click it. It starts with Windows and adds itself to the Start menu. `Maestro.exe --sair` closes a running instance and undoes its changes.

Settings live in %APPDATA%\Maestro\maestro.json (ExtraGames, NeverRestrain, SlowDuringGames, Medal, QBittorrentWebUi, Language, CheckUpdates, ShowFps) and reload on save; a broken file keeps the last good one. Logs in %LOCALAPPDATA%\Maestro\logs.
